thread:
maria_devex: Noticed a weird SSE ordering bug in the browser sample app when people flip offline/online quickly. Repro below.
kevin_sdk: hmm, ordering? we generally assume server-sent events arrive in order. Any chance chunks are getting merged or re-ordered by the client runtime?
joel_browser: captured a sequence where the network toggled during an active stream. Browser reported chunks arriving as: data: {"id":"a1","delta":"PartA1"}

data: {"id":"b1","delta":"PartB1"}

data: {"id":"a2","delta":"PartA2"}
The stream consumer concatenates by arrival order, and our reassembly expects a1->a2 then b1, but we got a1,b1,a2 which ends up producing garbled JSON when we merge pieces into messages.
sam_infra: server logs show events emitted in A1,A2,B1 order. So it's likely the browser fetch connection split and the intermediate fetch resumed with a chunk boundary that overlapped different logical message streams.
kevin_sdk: interesting. Is last-event-id set on events? we use last-event-id to resume; if it's not present for each logical message, resume logic can replay chunks or misapply them.
joel_browser: last-event-id is only set per logical message, but some intermediate fragments have no id since our runtime splits long payloads. When connection closes and we reconnect, the runtime concatenates low-level chunks without remapping them to logical message ids.
qa_bot: repro steps: 1) open sample app on Chrome 2) start streaming generation 3) toggle DevTools network offline for ~150ms then online 4) observe parse exceptions ~10-20% runs
maria_devex: users hit this when they switch networks on mobile browsers too. Bad UX.
kevin_sdk: short-term mitigation for sample app: treat incoming SSE fragments with an internal sequence buffer keyed by event-id when present; if absent, hold fragments until a full JSON object can be parsed (try/catch) and drop fragments that fail parse after 500ms with a log. That avoids merging unrelated fragments.
sam_infra: longer term: SDK should normalize chunking parity across runtimes. Node stream parser currently emits 'event' per data block; browser fetch stream may slice arbitrarily. We need a cross-SDK reassembly layer that inspects 'data:' markers and normalizes.
joel_browser: i'll open a tiny PR in the sample app to add the hold-until-parse heuristic so onboarding users don't hit crashes.
kevin_sdk: i'll add an SDK issue to implement a reassembly buffer and add tests for offline/online toggles and reordered arrivals. Also adding an e2e harness that simulates chunk interleaving.
qa_bot: created ticket #4599: "sse: reassembly buffer + offline-toggle tests" assigned to kevin_sdk.
maria_devex: thanks. Also add a short note in the sample app README: "If you see sporadic parse errors when toggling network, update to SDK X.Y or use sample app patch."
joel_browser: patch PR up in ~1h, requesting review from kevin_sdk and sam_infra.
kevin_sdk: will review. If the sample app fix looks safe we'll ship it to the quickstart so new users don't get blocked.
